title: LoopWeaver: Weaving Feedback Loops into Hierarchical Generation under Constraints
claim: A constrained generation task flows through staged planning, filtering, reward scoring, and preference-aligned generation to produce a structured final output.
layout: 7 boxed stages in snake order: top row left-to-right, bottom row right-to-left
description: A two-row flow diagram of seven rounded, color-coded boxes joined by thick black arrows. The top row runs left to right. It starts with 'Objective & Constraints', a community-garden goal with three typed constraints: Single, Range and Periodic. Next is 'Candidate Plans', a 2x2 grid of cartoon icons for plans A to D (vegetable, flower, mixed and leisure garden). Then comes 'Decision Filter', which marks plans A, B and D with red X marks and plan C with a green check, plus a 'Plan C: 0.8' box. An arrow turns down into the bottom row, which runs right to left. 'Reward Evaluation' has a trophy and a list of plan-representation features. 'Execution Generation' lists preference-aligned steps and the DPO-style inequality πθ(y+|x) > πθ(y−|x). The last box is 'Final Generation', with a robot mascot. Warm yellow and orange headers sit alongside blue ones.
caption: Constrained long-form generation in LoopWeaver with planning, generation, and verification.
abstract: Large Language Models face a multi-objective optimization problem in constrained long-text generation, balancing global structure, local coherence, and constraint satisfaction. We propose LoopWeaver, a hierarchical workflow with two sequential offline preference-optimization stages. Constraint-aware planning produces structured plans, feasibility filtering removes invalid plans, and a shared deterministic reward constructs preference pairs for plan-level and generation-level DPO. At inference time, LoopWeaver remains feed-forward: it generates and revises a complete plan, filters the revised plan, and then generates segments conditioned on the current sub-plan and running narrative. We evaluate the method on four LongGenBench-style structured scenarios across multiple backbones. Results show improvements in both constraint accuracy and text quality across all four open-source backbones. Our software and data are publicly available at https://github.com/cgtaa-cmyk/LoopWeaver.
